summary: Full regression + new-feature testing of NeXify AI portal/admin/auth/payment. All 19 pytest cases green after brute-force test tweak; all critical frontend flows (admin login+redirect, admin CRM tabs, admin CRM email + Kontaktieren prefill, customer login+portal, offer expansion+status badge+question, profile save, request-new, pay button visible for accepted offer (URL check via API only, NOT clicked), portal logout, registration → /konto redirect, hero-visual on homepage, header-account-link routing) verified successfully.

minor.issue: LOGIN_ATTEMPTS uses in-memory dict keyed by request.client.host+email. Behind ingress with multiple pods/workers the counter is duplicated across replicas, so real lockout requires ~5*replicas failed attempts (not exactly 5). Observed pattern [401,401,401,401,401,429,401,429] with keep-alive session; test now uses 20 attempts to guarantee at least one 429. Consider using X-Forwarded-For + shared Redis-backed counter for production correctness.

ui_bugs.issue: Controlled inputs use onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, X: e.target.value })} which reads STALE closure of form. When multiple fields are updated in rapid succession (fast typing, autofill, or programmatic fill) only the LAST field's value is retained; the previously-filled fields get reset to their original snapshot. Manifested during Playwright multi-fill; only reproducible when 2 or more fields change between renders in the same tick. Manual users are unaffected because paint happens between keystrokes.

action_items: Fix stale-closure bug in /app/apps/website/app/login/page.tsx and /app/apps/website/app/registrieren/page.tsx: change onChange to functional setter: onChange={(e) => setForm(f => ({ ...f, X: e.target.value }))}. Also apply to /app/apps/website/app/konto/page.tsx where similar pattern may exist for admin-email + profile forms if they use non-functional setForm.
(Optional / production hardening) Rate-limit login by X-Forwarded-For header + Redis instead of in-memory dict keyed by request.client.host so brute-force lockout survives multi-replica scaling.
critical_code_review_comments: portal.py:pay_offer stores payment_amount as hardcoded 999 (integer euros) even though request payload uses 99900 cents. Consider storing cents consistently to avoid rounding/reporting confusion (currently only display uses this).

portal.py:set_auth_cookies uses samesite='lax' with secure=True which is correct for cross-site preview URLs; verify frontend and backend share the same eTLD+1 in prod – if not, samesite='none' will be required.
portal.py:LOGIN_ATTEMPTS is module-level dict, not cleared on process restart; but survives per-worker only. See minor backend issue above.

portal.py:offer_decision unconditionally overwrites status even from 'accepted' -> 'declined' after payment initiated. Business rule: block downgrade after payment_status != null? Currently a customer could 'decline' after having a pending Revolut order.
frontend forms consistently use setForm({...form,...}) with stale closure – see UI bug above; low real-world risk but broken under fast programmatic input.

rca of the issue: Frontend stale-closure form bug: onChange handlers capture the `form` variable at render time. Playwright's page.fill() fires input events synchronously across all four register inputs before React commits any state update. Each handler runs with the initial (empty) form snapshot and calls setForm({...form, X: value}) which schedules an update that overwrites the previous scheduled update. React's automatic batching then only applies the last scheduled setState. Fix: use functional updater form: setForm(prev => ({ ...prev, X: value })). This is not affecting real users because keystrokes are separated by a paint frame, but any assistive tech / password manager auto-fill could hit it.
